newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends unchanged but mkt cautious.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends unchanged but mkt cautious.

text.p: *Central Bank raises overnight borrowing to 10.25 pct
The Philippine peso reversed early gains at the close on Friday as banks bought dollars on fears of more outflows from the stock market, dealers said.
It closed unchanged at 26.37 but down from the early morning deals of 26.368/26.367 when the Central Bank announced a 0.25 percentage-point hike in its overnight borrowing rate to 10.25 percent.
The rate increase had prompted banks to sell their dollars.
"However, the stock market was down again. Banks wanted to be cautious," a foreign bank dealer said.
The Central Bank lifted its overnight borrowing rate to support the local currency which had been under attack as financial markets were abuzz with talk the Philippines may be the next Thailand.
A property crash in Thailand had spilled over to their banks.
Traders estimated the Central Bank had to unload some $39 million at 26.37 in late deals to quell the attack on the peso.
However, the day's average was at 26.366 from the previous 26.369. Volume rose to $198.3 million from $178.1 million.
"Everyone will be waiting for what the Central Bank will do on Monday since the peso is still under attack," a trader said.
